interest: Rumors of Japanese bases in Baja California.
overview: This file (U.S. State Department decimal file 894.34512) spans from January 1931 to September 1938 and documents reports, tips, and diplomatic investigations concerning alleged Japanese naval, military, and espionage activities in Mexico, particularly in Baja California and the Gulf of California. The file opens with a 1931 cross-reference to historian Thomas A. Bailey's inquiries regarding Japanese designs on Magdalena Bay and a 1933 letter from a private citizen claiming knowledge of a secret Japanese naval base. The core of the file consists of September 1938 communications from American Consul Horatio Mooers in Mexicali, who reported intelligence from a Mexican fishing vessel operator regarding a Japanese submarine rendezvous near Ángel de la Guarda Island, proposed accompanying an observation cruise along the Gulf coast (which Assistant Secretary of State A. A. Berle, Jr. instructed him not to undertake), surveyed the size and influence of the local Japanese agricultural colony, and relayed claims by a former German officer that Japanese homesteads between Tijuana and Ensenada were built with reinforced concrete gun emplacements.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting correspondence from Thomas A. Bailey regarding rumored Japanese attempts to acquire land at Magdalena Bay, Mexico.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Thomas A. Bailey's 1931 letter on Japan and Magdalena Bay.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Letter from Thomas A. Bailey on Magdalena Bay

subfiles.about: Letter from a San Diego citizen offering confidential information concerning an alleged Japanese naval base in Lower California.
subfiles.summary: Harry Downes says he has proof of a Japanese naval base in Lower California.
subfiles.title: Letter from Harry Downes on Alleged Japanese Naval Base in Lower California

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum summarizing Consul Mooers's report of a Japanese submarine sighting in the Gulf of California and his offer to join a reconnaissance cruise.
subfiles.summary: Tanis summarizes Mooers's report of a Japanese submarine seen in the Gulf of California.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by R. C. Tanis on Reported Japanese Submarine in Gulf of California

subfiles.about: Confidential consular despatch reporting informant accounts of a Japanese submarine in the Gulf of California, possible hidden bases, and local Japanese activities.
subfiles.summary: Mooers reports a fisherman's sighting of a Japanese submarine in the Gulf of California and offers to join a scouting cruise.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 10 from Horatio Mooers on Possibility of Japanese Naval Base in Gulf of California

subfiles.about: Department of State instruction advising Consul Mooers against taking part in an undercover coastal observation cruise.
subfiles.summary: Berle tells Mooers not to join the proposed coastal cruise.
subfiles.title: Instruction from A. A. Berle, Jr., to Horatio Mooers on Proposed Observation Cruise

subfiles.about: Consular letter clarifying estimates of the Japanese population and investigating planned agricultural colonization in the Mexicali valley and Baja California.
subfiles.summary: Mooers revises the estimate of Japanese in Mexicali district to about 500 farmers.
subfiles.title: Letter from Horatio Mooers to James B. Stewart Regarding Japanese Population in Baja California

subfiles.about: Confidential consular despatch reporting corroboration of the submarine sighting and allegations of reinforced concrete artillery emplacements at Japanese homesteads.
subfiles.summary: Mooers reports more submarine sightings and claims of gun emplacements in Japanese homesteads near Ensenada.
subfiles.title: Despatch from Horatio Mooers on Japanese Activities and Alleged Gun Emplacements
